title: Timing, Metastability and Parallelism
toolchain: no code on screen. Check every inequality, worked number (clock periods, frequencies, latencies, throughputs), the MTBF example and any number you add, in Python 3.11.9, standard library only (math), solving the MTBF equation by bisection: `python3 -I check.py`. The planner's checks are in PLAN.md (Decisions, 'Checked numbers'). No HDL or circuit simulator is installed (iverilog, yosys, ghdl, verilator, ngspice: none).

sources.note: Slides for the whole course (190 pp., two slides per page). This lecture is pp. 104-119: set-up and hold constraints, contamination delay, clock skew, metastability, synchronisers and MTBF, parallelism and pipelining. p. 120 (the 'Synchronous State Machines 1' title) is only shown at the close: next-lecture teaser. pp. 101 (second slide)-103 (shift register, serial data link, system timing) belong to Lecture 7, which has no recording here; ch1 s2 and ch2 s3 re-teach the parts this lecture leans on. Already known: gate propagation delay p. 58, hazards and glitches pp. 59-62, timing diagrams p. 60, and Lecture 6 (pp. 85-101). pdftotext renders tau as 't' on pp. 111 and 114, and drops subscripts: read formulas from the rendered page (pdftoppm). p. 117's circuit: CB1 and CB2 in parallel, both feeding CB3, then CB4; point A is between CB3 and CB4
